To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reactivity and the stability of acyl-glucuronide metabolites are determined by the electronic and steric factors that influence their formation.
the stability of 1-O-glucuronide metabolites is dependent on electronic and steric factors and the electronic factor is dominant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the factors that influence the reactivity of acyl glucuronic acid conjugates.

the elucidation of the physicochemical properties of acyl glucuronic acid derivatives and their role in the stability of acyl conjugates, which may be important in the design of new drugs with reduced toxicity.
the development of structure–property relationships that can be used to predict and design drug molecules with improved metabolic stability and reduced toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stability of 1-O-glucuronides is a function of the electronic nature of the carbonyls and the steric bulk of the substituents on the carbonyl, with the electronic nature of these substituents being the dominant factor.
the stability and reactivity of 1-O-acetyl-β-d-gluronides is determined by a combination of the pKa of acyl carbonyls and the size and shape of the substituents about that carbonyl.

the more acidic the parent acid, the greater the stability of the conjugate and vice versa, with the stability of the acyl glucuronide decreasing with the addition of electron withdrawing groups and increasing steric hindrance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more acidic the carboxyl group in the drug, the more stable the acyl glucuronide metabolite.
, for a given drug, the more polar the parent drug, the more stable is the glucuronide.
the more stable acyl glucuronide is formed by the more reactive parent drug, the more stable the acyl glucuronidate is the less reactive the drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of the acyl glucuronide conjugate is dependent on both electronic and steric effects of the substituents about both the carboxyl and carbonyl carbon atoms.
the reactivity of acyl glucurinides can be predicted from the pKa of their parent acids.
the pKa of an acyl glucuronide conjugate is a function of the pKa of parent drug.
